title: How biomedical foundation models turn literature and other biological data into training corpora
timestamp_policy: Human-facing generation time is fixed PST (UTC-8). The directory date is the UTC research date.
scope: 31 model families, three training-data studies, three reusable corpora and four method references. Token counts are organized by direct online-paper acquisition, direct web acquisition and reused datasets, with original source units, count bases and disclosure gaps preserved.
method: Targeted web searches, citation following, and reading primary papers, official technical reports, and author repositories. This is a broad targeted review, not an exhaustive systematic census or a common-protocol model leaderboard. Unknown details remain unknown.
execution: Literature review and small source snapshots only. No new OCR, model inference, training, paid teacher generation, GPU allocation, or bulk paper collection. Existing experiments and scores are unchanged.
interpretation_rules: Corpus tokens, training tokens consumed, distinct papers, abstracts, packed sequences, and image-caption pairs are different units. Counts across models overlap and must not be added.
PMC-derived does not establish whether a model used XML, PDFs, or an upstream extraction. A missing OCR description is not evidence that OCR was never used upstream.

Continued pretraining (CPT) means additional language-model training on a domain corpus. Instruction tuning (SFT) means training on task prompts and target responses. Older papers sometimes call both fine-tuning.
A teacher's educational-quality score is a curation signal, not scientific truth or independently adjudicated extraction ground truth.
Published benchmark numbers below are author-reported and protocol-specific. They are not measurements from our 50-paper extraction experiment.
Clinical evidence ranking and exclusion of animal studies should not be copied into a corpus intended for biological research.
